locations.name: Franz Joseph
locations.description: The former Austro-Hungarian emperor lounging in a tiny hammock — a playful nod to the Liberty Bridge, originally named in his honour.

locations.name: Meerkat
locations.description: Commissioned by the Szurikáta Foundation for diabetic children; the meerkat's tiny backpack symbolizes the medical supplies diabetic kids carry.

locations.name: The Axe
locations.description: A bronze axe resting on a velvet pillow, a satirical response to the political vandalism that destroyed the original ushanka hat nearby.

locations.name: Dog Fair in Buda
locations.description: A basket of tiny dogs illustrating the famous Hungarian idiom 'Egyszer volt Budán kutyavásár' (There was only one dog fair in Buda).

locations.name: Jeanne d'Arc (Lisa Simpson)
locations.description: Lisa Simpson depicted tied to a stake like Joan of Arc; this recast replacement sits along the Tram 2 line after the original vanished.

locations.name: Ratatouille (Lecsó) Rat
locations.description: A life-sized bronze rat holding a spray can, painting 'lecsó' on a wall — a crossover homage to the Pixar film and the Hungarian stew.

locations.name: Vuk, the Fox
locations.description: The mischievous fox cub from István Fekete's classic, humorously shown holding on to a small bomb in the rock wall of Forrásbarlang.

locations.name: Footprint (Lábnyom)
locations.description: A Khanty hunter carrying a deer, perched on a rocky base — a philosophical reflection on humanity's ecological footprint.

locations.name: Balloon Dog (Libido)
locations.description: A balloon-animal dog sniffing at a bone near the Chain Bridge; a cheeky nod to Jeff Koons and Ilona Staller.

locations.name: Rubik's Cube
locations.description: A 27-element tribute to Ernő Rubik's world-famous Hungarian invention, placed across from the Parliament. There is always a solution.

locations.name: Nincs kompót
locations.description: A miniature pantry with a tiny working door and an empty jam jar, referencing a catchphrase from the 1965 satirical film.

locations.name: Rabbit with Checkered Ears
locations.description: The iconic 1970s cartoon rabbit peering through binoculars at the funicular's upper station — probably the hardest to miss.

locations.name: Dead Squirrel
locations.description: A tiny squirrel on its back beside a toy gun, a mock crime scene placed right next to Detective Columbo.

locations.name: Trabant
locations.description: A limestone mini Trabant with a wind-up key on its side, honoring the iconic East German people's car.

locations.name: Paddington & Masha's Bear
locations.description: Paddington Bear sitting on the belly of the bear from Masha and the Bear, installed on Christmas Eve — fitting for Bear Street.

locations.name: Skála Kópé
locations.description: The nostalgic 1980s commercial mascot on a modern chair, his glowing red heart on the outside of his chest.

locations.name: Sad Tank
locations.description: A harmless, drooping-barrel toy tank at the former Kossuth Bridge site, commemorating the 1956 Hungarian Revolution.

locations.name: Lunar Roving Vehicle
locations.description: Honors Hungarian-American NASA engineer Ferenc Pavlics, who designed the Apollo rover wheels — fittingly on 'Moon Street'.

locations.name: Ferenc Liszt
locations.description: The legendary composer sitting atop his vintage luggage at the airport named after him, unveiled on his 200th birthday.

locations.name: Kermit the Frog
locations.description: The beloved Muppet sitting at the base of a green fence; locals often dress him in tiny handmade winter scarves.

locations.name: Message (Russian Warship)
locations.description: A tiny Putin inside a Russian warship on a stone hand, a stark political statement from the Ukrainian-born artist.

locations.name: Scuba Diver
locations.description: An old-fashioned deep-sea diver holding a massive skeleton key, referencing the legend of the New York Café's key thrown to the Danube.

locations.name: Money Blower
locations.description: A worker with a leaf blower scattering pengő banknotes, marking the 1946 hyperinflation and the forint's anniversary.

locations.name: Leo and Fred
locations.description: Leo the lazy circus lion and his trainer Fred resting beside their trailer at the Kopaszi Dam amphitheater steps.

locations.name: Aranka Néni and Béla Bácsi
locations.description: A local elderly couple who ran a beloved flower stall at Pasaréti Square for decades, seated atop a blooming concrete flower.

locations.name: In Vino Veritas
locations.description: A tipsy Roman legionary beside an empty wine jug at the Aquincum amphitheatre; its twin stands in the Colosseum in Pula.

locations.name: Draft Horses
locations.description: Two draft horses pulling a cart of beer barrels, commissioned for the Dreher Brewery's anniversary.

locations.name: Antal Dreher
locations.description: The brewery founder atop a wooden beer barrel leaning on a walking stick, inside the Dreher Brewery courtyard.

locations.name: Hanna Szenes
locations.description: The WWII Jewish poet and British paratrooper taking a leap of faith over a limestone map of Hungary, in the park named for her.

locations.name: Rezső Seress
locations.description: The composer of 'Gloomy Sunday', who spent decades playing piano at this very restaurant on Akácfa Street.

locations.name: Noah's Ark
locations.description: A miniature ark on a stone pillar near the Veterinary University; peek through its tiny windows to spot a painted rainbow.

locations.name: Fourteen Carat Car
locations.description: A bronze Alfa Romeo honoring pulp-fiction writer Jenő Rejtő and his novel 'The Fourteen-Carat Car', near the author's birthplace.

locations.name: Theodor Herzl
locations.description: The father of modern political Zionism sitting on a bicycle, right by the Dohány Street Synagogue near his birthplace.

locations.name: Mekk Elek
locations.description: The bumbling handyman goat from Hungarian puppet animation, holding a plaque referencing 'Moscow Square', the former name of the hub.

locations.name: Winnie the Pooh
locations.description: The honey-loving bear reaching upward, on the facade of Frigyes Karinthy's birthplace — who named the bear after his sister's nickname.

locations.name: Chief Worm
locations.description: Kolodko's very first mini-sculpture in Hungary — the cheerful fishing bait from The Great Ho-Ho Angler — with a great Danube view.

locations.name: Miksa Róth
locations.description: A rare indoor piece showing Hungary's master stained-glass and mosaic artist holding a delicate glass pane, in his memorial house.

locations.name: Harry Houdini
locations.description: A rare indoor sculpture in the K11 Cultural Center lobby commemorating the illusionist's birthplace in Budapest.

locations.name: Headphones
locations.description: A functional pair of miniature bronze headphones outside Müpa that quietly plays classical music when you lean in.

locations.name: Empire (Queen Elizabeth II)
locations.description: The queen in her hat and handbag atop a Yellow Submarine, in Millenáris Park — a nod to the Beatles' MBE moment.

locations.name: Garfield
locations.description: A colorful, painted Garfield on the Veterinary University's brick fence, created for the cat's 45th birthday.

locations.name: Piszkos Fred (Dirty Fred)
locations.description: Jenő Rejtő's slippery pulp-fiction adventurer beside a ship's chest, next to the Hungarian Academy of Sciences.

locations.name: Tied-Up Chuck Norris
locations.description: The action hero tied up on the Megyeri Bridge, a nod to the 2006 internet vote to name it the 'Chuck Norris Bridge'.

locations.name: Lucky Saint Nicholas
locations.description: A miniature Saint Nicholas designed to bring good luck, tucked inside the Erzsébetligeti Theatre foyer.

locations.name: Yoda
locations.description: The wise Jedi Master in deep contemplation, perched on the handrail at the top of the escalators in Szent Gellért Square M4.

locations.name: Pinocchio
locations.description: Pinocchio with a remarkably long wooden nose, unveiled near the Hungarian Academy of Sciences / Vigadó embankment.

locations.name: Dr. Bubó & the Nervous Rabbit
locations.description: Dr. Bubó the owl-doctor and his anxious rabbit patient 'opened a clinic' on the Bethesda Children's Hospital fence.

locations.name: Vilmos Zsigmondy
locations.description: The 19th-century mining engineer who drilled the City Park artesian well feeding the Széchenyi Bath, shown relaxing.
